title: The referral operations, their fields, the referral state set, the Aric interface, the record codes and the right of a fraud referral are not in the sources
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-018); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.29, VR-P4-029-1, BR-P4-029, A2.7, requirements served); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T1, T2, T3.1, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, T6.3, appendix T-A); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md (INT-31); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-UNI-08, R-DEV-04, R-DEV-13, R-LIT-77, R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39); _work/msr/context/P4.md (ownership rows of rwb-access)
description: Five groups of values of this legacy key are not in the sources. (1) The referral operations: the FSD A2.29 names the journey and names no operation, and appendix T-A of TSD P4 v3 lists no fraud-referral path, so the two paths, the request and the answer fields and the identifier are fixed by this story's contract. (2) The Aric interface: INT-31 gives the direction, the frequency and the statement 'not available today' and no base URL, no media type, no authentication and no field of the request or the answer, and this story's dependency rows carry no rwb-integration contract even though DP-16 places the outbound adapter with P2. (3) The referral state set and the record codes: no source names a lifecycle of a referral, and none names the record code of a referral entry or of its outcome entry in the local decision-record chain. (4) The right: the legacy permission table gives Rules and parameters C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK, which belong to the rule-version template rows of the legacy story, TSD P4 v3 T6.1 publishes three of the 14 capability areas only, and no source says which area and which letter a fraud referral needs. (5) The screen and the requirement: the panel that carries the referral is not named in any source, and no P4 requirement names a fraud referral at all. The value of the rule version is not a gap: R-UNI-38 and the FSD step that reads the version in force make it a label carried on the referral, and this story records the label it is given rather than reading a rule table.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.29 gives one business rule (BR-P4-029), one validation rule (VR-P4-029-1), the roles table (unattended primary, fraud investigator also uses) and AC-P4-029-01 with no field, no state and no operation; TSD P4 v3 T-A lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 with no referral path, T3.1 lists the access tables (role, permission, delegation_limit, lov_value) and no referral table, T5.3 gives rwb-access no event, and T6.1 publishes the letters of Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration only; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 lists INT-31 Aric, fraud referral, outbound, 'not available today; by the fraud investigator'; the context pack lists the four provided operations of P4 (GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants) and no referral operation; the legacy story RWB-E8-018 carries the rule-version endpoints and the rule-versions base of the monolith, which are the rule registry's and not this feature's; the Business Rules and Routing Logic gives the four routing rules that read the outcome and no shape of a referral.
proposed: Fix the two operations on /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/fraud-referrals in RWB-P4-E8018-CON with the request and answer fields of section 11; declare the Aric interface as an external operation consumed through a port and its fake, with the missing rwb-integration contract raised at D1 and not added to the metadata; fix the three referral states REFERRED, ANSWERED and FAILED and the terminal outcome; record the referral and its outcome as two entries of the local DP-03 chain under the library's referral codes settled with the ledger owner; read the right of the referral as a permission row in Case record C and R, confirmed by the access owner; and fix the panel identifier with the gateway-bff contract owner.

title: The contract baseline has to fix the Aric request and answer shape, the referral state set and the record codes because no source states them
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-018); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.29); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.1, T6.1, T6.3, appendix T-A); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md (INT-31); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-DEV-13, R-LIT-77, R-UNI-39); _work/msr/context/P4.md
description: The contract baseline publishes four things that no source fixes: the Aric request and answer shape beyond the referral key and the confirmation; the statement that a referral has exactly three states and that an outcome is terminal; the record codes of the referral entry and of its outcome entry, and the field-level placement of a referral inside the record's inputs_ref; and the identifiers the document declares, since no operation of this feature appears in appendix T-A and no event of rwb-access carries the outcome. The confirmation is modelled as one boolean and no outcome code vocabulary is invented, because the sources name no code set and two routing rules read the confirmation; that reading is itself a default and is recorded here.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.29 gives one sentence of description per step and no field of the exchange; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 lists the access tables and the standard record columns of T3.0 and no referral table, T6.3 fixes the append-only change log and names no code of an administrative or external referral, and T-A carries no referral operation; INT-31 gives Aric as an outbound fraud referral that is not available today with no interface detail; the Business Rules and Routing Logic give R-DEV-13 and R-LIT-77 reading 'fraud confirmed in Aric' with no vocabulary and R-UNI-39 for the unlogged action; the context pack gives rwb-access no event of its own.
proposed: Publish the baseline with the two operations, both schemas, the three-state closed set, the boolean confirmation and the consumed Aric interface, each open value marked with the placeholder of Template and Rules section R9; settle the Aric field detail with the Aric owner and rwb-integration, the record codes with the ledger owner and the panel identifier with the gateway-bff owner before the baseline is tagged; and add the missing dependencies at D1 rather than changing the metadata rows of the Work Package.
